title: How to Handle Content Form Requests with Resend and Cosmic
summary: Build a content request form that saves submissions in Cosmic and sends instant email notifications and confirmations with Resend.
body_markdown:
Content request forms come up in almost every app. Someone asks for a case study, a guest post, a product page update or a press kit. Your team needs to see the request, track it and reply quickly. This guide shows how to combine two tools to handle it: - **Cosmic** stores each request as structured content your team can review, edit and track in the dashboard. - **Resend** sends an instant notification to your team and a confirmation email to the person who submitted it. We'll use a Next.js App Router project, but the same pattern works in any framework that can run server-side code. ## How it works 1. A visitor fills out a content request form. 2. The form posts to a server route in your app. 3. The route saves the request as a new object in Cosmic. 4. The route uses Resend to email your team and confirm receipt to the requester. Your API keys stay on the server, and every request gets a durable record in your CMS, even if an email fails. ## 1. Set up your content model in Cosmic In your Cosmic bucket, create an object type called **Content Requests** (slug` content-requests` ) with these metafields: Key Type ` requester_name` Text ` requester_email` Text ` request_type` Select (Blog post, Case study, Page update, Other) ` details` Textarea ` status` Select (New, In progress, Done) The` status` field lets your editors move requests through a simple workflow right in the dashboard. ## 2. Install the SDKs ```text npm install @cosmicjs/sdk resend ``` Add your keys to` .env.local` : ```text COSMIC_BUCKET_SLUG = your-bucket-slug COSMIC_READ_KEY = your-read-key COSMIC_WRITE_KEY = your-write-key RESEND_API_KEY = re_xxxxxxxxx NOTIFY_EMAIL = content-team@yourdomain.com ``` You can find your Cosmic keys under your bucket's API access settings, and your Resend key in the Resend dashboard. Make sure the domain you send from is verified in Resend. ## 3. Create the API route Create` app/api/content-request/route.ts` : ```text import { NextResponse } from 'next/server' import { createBucketClient } from '@cosmicjs/sdk' import { Resend } from 'resend' const cosmic = createBucketClient ( { bucketSlug : process . env . COSMIC_BUCKET_SLUG ! , readKey : process . env . COSMIC_READ_KEY ! , writeKey : process . env . COSMIC_WRITE_KEY ! , } ) const resend = new Resend ( process . env . RESEND_API_KEY ) export async function POST ( request : Request ) { const { name , email , requestType , details } = await request . json ( ) if ( ! name || ! email || ! details ) { return NextResponse . json ( { error : 'Missing required fields' } , { status : 400 } ) } // 1. Save the request in Cosmic const { object } = await cosmic . objects . insertOne ( { type : 'content-requests' , title : ` ${ requestType } : ${ name } ` , status : 'draft' , metadata : { requester_name : name , requester_email : email , request_type : requestType , details , status : 'New' , } , } ) // 2. Notify your team and confirm with the requester await Promise . all ( [ resend . emails . send ( { from : 'Content Requests ' , to : process . env . NOTIFY_EMAIL ! , replyTo : email , subject : ` New content request: ${ requestType } ` , html : `

${ name } ( ${ email } ) requested a ${ requestType } .

${ details }

Cosmic object ID: ${ object . id }

` , } ) , resend . emails . send ( { from : 'Content Team ' , to : email , subject : 'We received your content request' , html : `

Hi ${ name } ,

Thanks for your request. Our team will review it and get back to you soon.

` , } ) , ] ) return NextResponse . json ( { success : true } ) } ``` A few notes: - Saving to Cosmic first means you never lose a request, even if an email fails to send. - Setting` replyTo` to the requester's email lets your team reply straight from their inbox. - In production, escape user input before putting it in HTML, or use React Email templates with Resend. ## 4. Build the form ```text 'use client' import { useState } from 'react' export default function ContentRequestForm ( ) { const [ status , setStatus ] = useState < 'idle' | 'sending' | 'sent' | 'error' > ( 'idle' ) async function handleSubmit ( e : React . FormEvent < HTMLFormElement > ) { e . preventDefault ( ) setStatus ( 'sending' ) const form = new FormData ( e . currentTarget ) const res = await fetch ( '/api/content-request' , { method : 'POST' , headers : { 'Content-Type' : 'application/json' } , body : JSON . stringify ( Object . fromEntries ( form ) ) , } ) setStatus ( res . ok ? 'sent' : 'error' ) } if ( status === 'sent' ) return < p > Thanks! Check your inbox for a confirmation. return ( < form onSubmit = { handleSubmit } > < input name = " name " placeholder = " Your name " required /> < input name = " email " type = " email " placeholder = " you@company.com " required /> < select name = " requestType " > < option > Blog post < option > Case study < option > Page update < option > Other < textarea name = " details " placeholder = " Tell us what you need " required /> < button disabled = { status === 'sending' } > { status === 'sending' ? 'Sending…' : 'Submit request' } { status === 'error' && < p > Something went wrong. Please try again. } ) } ``` ## 5. Go further with status updates Once requests are in Cosmic, you can close the loop automatically. Set up a Cosmic webhook that fires when a content request is edited, and point it at another route in your app. When an editor changes` status` to **Done** , that route can use Resend to tell the requester their content is live. Now your editors work in the CMS, and your requesters stay informed without anyone writing a manual email. ## Wrapping up With a single API route, you get: - A structured, searchable record of every content request in Cosmic - Instant team notifications and requester confirmations from Resend - A base for automated status updates Start by verifying a sending domain in Resend and creating your Content Requests type in Cosmic. You can ship this in an afternoon.
